title: Ezekiel Chapter 20 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 20 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 20 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 20.

questions.question: Who came to enquire of the LORD in Ezekiel 20?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:1 states that 'certain of the elders of Israel came to enquire of the LORD.'

questions.question: What did the LORD say He would not do concerning the elders of Israel?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 20:3, the LORD states, 'I will not be enquired of by you.'

questions.question: What does the LORD command the elders to know?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:4 asks them to 'cause them to know the abominations of their fathers.'

questions.question: In which land did the LORD make Himself known to Israel?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:5 mentions that the LORD made Himself known unto them in the land of Egypt.

questions.question: What did the LORD promise to bring Israel into?
options: A land flowing with milk and honey
questions.correctAnswer: A land flowing with milk and honey
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:6 describes the land as 'flowing with milk and honey, which is the glory of all lands.'

questions.question: True or False: The Israelites cast away the abominations of their eyes and forsook the idols of Egypt.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:8 states that they 'did not every man cast away the abominations of their eyes, neither did they forsake the idols of Egypt.'

questions.question: What did the LORD say He would do because of Israel's rebellion?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:8 mentions that the LORD said, 'I will pour out my fury upon them.'

questions.question: True or False: The LORD gave Israel His statutes and judgments.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:11 states, 'I gave them my statutes, and shewed them my judgments.'

questions.question: What did the LORD give to Israel as a sign between Him and them?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:12 indicates that He gave them 'my sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them.'

questions.question: What consequence did the LORD mention for those who despised His judgments?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:13 states that the LORD would pour out His fury upon them for their rebellion.

questions.question: True or False: The children of Israel walked in the statutes of their fathers.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:21 explains that they 'walked not in my statutes, neither kept my judgments.'

questions.question: In Ezekiel 20, what comes first when the LORD speaks to the house of Israel?
options: He commands them to keep His statutes
He asks them if they are polluted after their fathers
He reminds them of their rebellion
He tells them to offer sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: He asks them if they are polluted after their fathers
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:30 is where the LORD asks, 'Are ye polluted after the manner of your fathers?'

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 20 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 20 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the elders of Israel do in Ezekiel 20:1?
options: They came to enquire of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They came to enquire of the LORD
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:1 states, 'And it came to pass in the seventh year, in the fifth month, the tenth day of the month, that certain of the elders of Israel came to enquire of the LORD, and sat before me.' This shows that they sought guidance from God.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 20:3, what does the Lord say about being enquired of by the elders?
options: He will not be enquired of by them
questions.correctAnswer: He will not be enquired of by them
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 20:3, the Lord states, 'As I live, saith the Lord GOD, I will not be enquired of by you.' This indicates God's refusal to engage with them due to their disobedience.

questions.question: What did God command the people to do in Ezekiel 20:7?
options: Cast away every man the abominations of his eyes
Follow the statutes of their fathers
Offer sacrifices in the high places
questions.correctAnswer: Cast away every man the abominations of his eyes
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:7 states, 'Then said I unto them, Cast ye away every man the abominations of his eyes, and defile not yourselves with the idols of Egypt: I am the LORD your God.' This highlights God's demand for purity among His people.

questions.question: What consequence did God declare in Ezekiel 20:8 for the people's rebellion?
options: He would pour out His fury upon them
He would lead them to the Promised Land
questions.correctAnswer: He would pour out His fury upon them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:8 shows God's anger: 'Then I said, I will pour out my fury upon them, to accomplish my anger against them in the midst of the land of Egypt.' This emphasizes the seriousness of their disobedience.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 20:12, what sign did God give to the people?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:12 states, 'Moreover also I gave them my sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them, that they might know that I am the LORD that sanctify them.' This shows the significance of the sabbaths in their relationship with God.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the children of Israel in the wilderness according to Ezekiel 20:21?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:21 notes, 'Notwithstanding the children rebelled against me: they walked not in my statutes, neither kept my judgments to do them.' This indicates their continued disobedience.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 20:23 indicate about God's intentions for the people?
options: He would bring them into the land of Canaan
He would scatter them among the heathen
He would bless them in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: He would scatter them among the heathen
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:23 states, 'I lifted up mine hand unto them also in the wilderness, that I would scatter them among the heathen, and disperse them through the countries.' This shows the consequences of their rebellion.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 20:25 say about the statutes given to the people?
options: They were meant for the priests only
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:25 states, 'Wherefore I gave them also statutes that were not good, and judgments whereby they should not live.' This reflects God's judgment on their persistent rebellion.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 20:31, what did the people do with their gifts?
options: They polluted themselves with their idols
They shared them with the poor
questions.correctAnswer: They polluted themselves with their idols
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:31 states, 'For when ye offer your gifts, when ye make your sons to pass through the fire, ye pollute yourselves with all your idols, even unto this day.' This highlights their corrupt practices.

questions.question: True or False: God promised to gather His people with a mighty hand according to Ezekiel 20:34.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:34 states, 'And I will bring you out from the people, and will gather you out of the countries wherein ye are scattered, with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out.' This shows God's commitment to His people.

questions.question: True or False: The people of Israel consistently obeyed God's statutes in the wilderness according to Ezekiel 20:21.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:21 indicates that 'the children rebelled against me: they walked not in my statutes,' showing that they did not obey God's commands.

questions.question: True or False: In Ezekiel 20:30, God asked the people if they were polluted after the manner of their fathers.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:30 confirms this: 'Wherefore say unto the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Are ye polluted after the manner of your fathers?' This shows God's awareness of their sinful behavior.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 20:36 teach about God's approach to His people?
options: He will plead with them face to face
He will punish them without reason
questions.correctAnswer: He will plead with them face to face
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:36 states, 'Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so will I plead with you,' indicating God's desire for reconciliation.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 20 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 20.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He will do with those who rebel against Him according to Ezekiel 20:38?
options: Bring them into the land of Israel
questions.explanation: The LORD states He will purge out from among them the rebels and those that transgress against Him (Ezekiel 20:38).

questions.question: In Ezekiel 20:41, what will the LORD do when He gathers His people from the countries?
questions.explanation: The LORD promises to be sanctified in the people before the heathen when He gathers them (Ezekiel 20:41).

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'wilderness of the people' mentioned in Ezekiel 20:35?
questions.explanation: The 'wilderness of the people' signifies a place where the LORD will plead with His people face to face, indicating a gathering (Ezekiel 20:35).

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 20:39, what does the LORD command the house of Israel to do?
questions.explanation: The LORD instructs them not to pollute His holy name anymore with their gifts and idols (Ezekiel 20:39).

questions.question: What literary device is evident in the repeated phrase 'I am the LORD' found throughout Ezekiel 20?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'I am the LORD' is a form of repetition used to emphasize God's identity and authority (Ezekiel 20:20, 20:26, etc.).

questions.question: In Ezekiel 20:42, what do the people of Israel recognize when brought into the land?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that they will remember their ways and loathe themselves for their evils committed (Ezekiel 20:43).

questions.question: Ezekiel 20:44 states that the people will know the LORD when He works with them. How does this connect to Jeremiah 31:34?
options: They will not remember their sins
questions.explanation: Both verses emphasize that the people will have a renewed understanding of the LORD and His ways (Ezekiel 20:44, Jeremiah 31:34).

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 20:46 instruct the prophet to do?
options: Prophesy against the forest of the south field
questions.correctAnswer: Prophesy against the forest of the south field
questions.explanation: The LORD commands Ezekiel to set his face toward the south and prophesy against the forest of the south field (Ezekiel 20:46).

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 20:47, what will the LORD kindle in the forest of the south?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD will kindle a fire that will devour every green and dry tree (Ezekiel 20:47).

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 20:21 states that the children of Israel did not rebel against the LORD.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:21 indicates that the children rebelled against the LORD, walking not in His statutes and polluting His sabbaths (Ezekiel 20:21).

questions.question: True or False: In Ezekiel 20:36, the LORD promises to plead with the people as He did with their fathers in Egypt.
questions.explanation: The LORD states that He will plead with them in the wilderness, just as He pleaded with their fathers in Egypt (Ezekiel 20:36).

questions.question: What does the phrase 'pass under the rod' in Ezekiel 20:37 signify in relation to the covenant?
questions.explanation: The phrase signifies bringing them into the bond of the covenant, indicating acceptance and belonging (Ezekiel 20:37).

questions.question: How does the theme of idolatry in Ezekiel 20:31 connect to Revelation 21:8?
questions.explanation: Both passages highlight the serious consequences for idolaters, indicating that they will not inherit the kingdom (Ezekiel 20:31, Revelation 21:8).

questions.question: What is the significance of the sabbath as mentioned in Ezekiel 20:20?
questions.explanation: The sabbath is described as a sign between God and His people, indicating the covenant relationship (Ezekiel 20:20).

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 20 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 20 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 20:3 reveal about God's willingness to be enquired of by the elders of Israel?
options: He is always eager to answer
He will not be enquired of by them
questions.correctAnswer: He will not be enquired of by them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:3 states that God will not be enquired of by the elders, indicating His refusal to engage with their insincere requests. This reflects His sovereignty and the importance of genuine repentance before seeking His guidance.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 20:8, how did the people respond to God's commands?
options: They rebelled and did not cast away idols
questions.correctAnswer: They rebelled and did not cast away idols
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:8 notes that the Israelites rebelled against God and did not forsake the idols of Egypt, illustrating their persistent disobedience and idolatry despite God's clear commands.

questions.question: What did God do for His name's sake as described in Ezekiel 20:9?
options: He brought Israel out of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: He brought Israel out of Egypt
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 20:9, God acted for His name's sake to ensure that it would not be polluted among the heathen, highlighting His commitment to His reputation and His covenant people.

questions.question: What is the significance of the sabbaths mentioned in Ezekiel 20:12?
options: They are a sign between God and Israel
They are for the priests only
questions.correctAnswer: They are a sign between God and Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:12 indicates that the sabbaths serve as a sign between God and His people, emphasizing the concept of sanctification and the special relationship between God and Israel.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 20:21 reveal about the behavior of the children of Israel?
options: They rebelled and polluted God's sabbaths
questions.correctAnswer: They rebelled and polluted God's sabbaths
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:21 illustrates that the children of Israel also rebelled against God, failing to keep His statutes and thus continuing the cycle of disobedience.

questions.question: What doctrine is illustrated by God's promise to gather His people as stated in Ezekiel 20:34?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:34 demonstrates God's sovereignty as He promises to gather His people from the nations with a mighty hand, showing His control over history and destiny.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 20:37 depict God's relationship with Israel?
options: As a ruler who enforces law
As a loving father who pleads
questions.correctAnswer: As a loving father who pleads
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:37 shows God pleading with Israel, which highlights His desire for reconciliation and a relationship built on covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What characterizes the judgments given to Israel in Ezekiel 20:25?
options: They were perfect and without fault
They were not good and led to death
They were only for the priests
questions.correctAnswer: They were not good and led to death
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:25 states that the statutes given were not good, indicating a divine judgment against Israel's rebellion, which led them further into sin.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 20:44 imply about God's actions in relation to His people?
options: He acts based on their righteousness
He acts for His name's sake
questions.correctAnswer: He acts for His name's sake
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:44 emphasizes that God acts for His name's sake, underscoring His commitment to His covenant and the importance of His reputation among the nations.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 20:30 question regarding the people's behavior?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:30 challenges the house of Israel about their pollution and idolatry, connecting their actions to the sinful ways of their ancestors.

questions.question: What is God's response to the rebellion of Israel in Ezekiel 20:17?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:17 indicates that despite their rebellion, God spared the Israelites from destruction, highlighting His mercy and patience.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 20:26 reveal about God's judgment on Israel's offerings?
options: They were polluted by their actions
They were for the priests only
questions.correctAnswer: They were polluted by their actions
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:26 reveals that God polluted the offerings of Israel because they were made while engaging in idolatry, showcasing the seriousness of their sin.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 20:42 relate to the concept of remembrance in Israel's history?
options: They will remember their ways and be ashamed
questions.correctAnswer: They will remember their ways and be ashamed
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:42 indicates that Israel will remember their defilements and loathe themselves, emphasizing the need for repentance and recognition of their sins.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 20:41 indicate about God's acceptance of offerings?
options: They are rejected due to sin
They are accepted when brought in faith
They are only for the high priest
questions.correctAnswer: They are accepted when brought in faith
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:41 suggests that God will accept the offerings of His people when they are gathered and sanctified, highlighting the importance of holiness in worship.

questions.question: What does the term 'Bamah' in Ezekiel 20:29 signify?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 20:29 refers to 'Bamah' as a high place where the Israelites went to worship idols, indicating their departure from true worship of God.
